editorial_candidates.reason: The item proves a concrete 4-regular Bruhat–Tits tree and describes how galleries branch into three forward choices at each extension. A small rooted neighborhood could make the type alternation and orbit-size growth immediate to inspect. The prose and proof already specify the geometry; no rendering or mathematical defect was seen.
editorial_candidates.diagram_data: Draw the base oriented edge E=([L0],[L1]) with type-0 then type-1 endpoints. At each step extend an edge gallery by changing endpoints alternately (labels s1 then s0); from each continuing edge draw its one backward edge and three forward edges, for total valency 4. Mark depth-n edge galleries by alternating word of length n and annotate each orbit size 3^n; distinguish this schematic orbit tree from the apartment chain L0,L1,L2,... and its opposite L1,L0,L−1,... .
editorial_candidates.checks: At every vertex there are four neighboring lattice classes, corresponding to the four lines in F3^2. Away from the base edge, one neighbor is the unique predecessor and the other three are successors. Endpoint types alternate along an edge gallery. A depth-n alternating word has 3^n edges; distinct words give distinct I-orbits and hence the stated double cosets. The schematic must not imply each individual orbit is a single apartment segment.
